items.title: Shanto: 'We have to do consistently well to go to the next level'
items.summary: "There is certainly a lack of capability," Shanto said after Bangladesh lost the second Test by an innings and 219 runs

items.title: Hridoy 'the best thing to come out of the series' as Tigers hit familiar South Africa low
items.summary: Bangladesh’s two-Test tour of South Africa ended in familiar, painful fashion on Wednesday, with the Tigers crashing to an innings-and-219-run defeat on Day 3 of the second Test in Centurion.

items.title: Centurion Test in numbers: Tigers' misery, Mulder's masterclass
items.summary: After folding for just 91 in the first innings, the visitors managed only 184 in reply, failing to produce a single half-century across the match. Their bowlers, meanwhile, had no answer to South Africa's imposing 494 for seven.

items.title: Tigers' tale: Another heavy defeat, same old hunt for positives
items.summary: And, as has become something of a recurring habit, Bangladesh were left looking for individual positives from a series in which the team collectively had very little to celebrate.

items.title: Seven-star Mulder leads South Africa to 2-0 whitewash
items.summary: The allrounder's century and seven-wicket haul helped South Africa inflict an innings defeat on Bangladesh

items.title: Bangladesh battered as Proteas complete 2-0 series sweep
items.summary: The defeat also pushed Bangladesh down to sixth in the World Test Championship standings, with their points percentage dropping to 36.67.

items.title: Ackerman, Mulder tons grind down Bangladesh as SA batters make hay
items.summary: Tony de Zorzi and Marco Jansen also hit fifties as South Africa added 406 runs on the second day

items.title: Shoriful admits Bangladesh's pace attack 'lacked discipline'

items.title: South Africa dominate after bowling Bangladesh out for 91
